newsitem.title: KUWAIT: State plans Kuwait Airways selloff.
newsitem.headline: State plans Kuwait Airways selloff.

text.p: Kuwait plans to transform state-owned Kuwait Airways Corp (KAC) into a shareholder company as a first step towards privatising the national flag carrier, al-Anba newspaper reported on Tuesday.
It said it had obtained a copy of a "bill that the government will submit to parliament in March to turn KAC into a Kuwaiti shareholder company in preparation for privatising it".

The document sets the capital of the new firm, Kuwait Airways Company, at 350 million dinars ($1.16 billion) divided into 3.5 billion shares of 100 fils which the state has the right of selling to Kuwaiti investors only.
The bill requires approval by parliament before sending it to the Emir, Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah, for ratification.
KAC has two new Boeing Co 777s on order to replace two Boeing 747s currently in service. It also operates 15 Airbus Industrie aircraft.
Since 1994 Kuwait has sold its stake in some 18 local firms for over $2 billion in the first phase of a privatisation plan, while 36 more worth some $3 billion still remain, officials say.
The government hopes to gain parliamentary approval in 1997 to start the next and more controversial stage of privatising public utilities such as water, electricity and health care.
